title: Add lexical-variance prober CI adapter for prompt sensitivity smokechecks
author: Maria Chen
release_notes: Adds a CI adapter that probes prompt sets with lightweight lexical perturbations (typos, whitespace, casing, synonym swaps) to surface brittle prompts and regressions. Ships disabled by default and gated behind a project-level opt-in flag.
description: Motivation: We frequently see regressions that only surface when prompts are slightly altered (typos, spacing, casing, small synonym swaps). These brittle prompts lead to production quality regressions that escape standard semantic checks. This PR adds a Lexical Variance Prober (LVP) CI adapter that runs a configurable suite of lightweight textual perturbations against existing prompt sets during CI smokechecks and reports sensitivity scores per-prompt and per-cohort. Design: LVP is implemented as a CI adapter that can be enabled per-eval-config and integrated into existing smoke gate pipelines. It generates a small set of perturbed inputs for each prompt using deterministic RNG seeds, runs model evaluations in parallel with budgeted sampling, computes a normalized sensitivity score (0-1) using token-level edit distances and semantic drift metrics, and annotates failing prompts when sensitivity exceeds configured thresholds. The adapter stores concise artifact summaries (CSV/JSON) and uploads a lightweight HTML report to the CI job artifacts for human triage. Compatibility and safety: The prober only uses non-invasive perturbations and avoids semantic rephrases that alter instruction intent by more than a configurable semantic-similarity threshold. It's disabled by default for older eval configs and can be opted-in via eval_config.enable_lexical_prober=true. CI integration: Adds a new job eval-lexical-prober in the smoke pipeline that runs under a :memory: budget with timeout guardrails and retries. The job is soft-fail by default for the first rollout and can be promoted to hard-gate by project teams. Metrics and outputs: The adapter emits per-prompt sensitivity, cohort-aggregated percentile, and a small failure set of highest-sensitivity prompts. These are tagged into existing CI telemetry so dashboards can trend sensitivity over time. Tests and validation: Unit tests cover perturbation generators and scoring functions, end-to-end integration runs against a synthetic prompt corpus in CI, and a canary run was executed against the 'paraphrase' and 'instructions' prompt cohorts. Performance: The prober adds ~12s median overhead to a smoke pipeline run for a typical 50-prompt smoke set due to parallelized execution and bounded sampling. Configs and docs: Added config schema docs, a short README with recommended thresholds, and a migration note for teams that want to adopt the prober. Rollout plan: Start as opt-in for two weeks while collecting telemetry, then recommend opt-in for all non-experimental eval configs. Related: ENG-1459 tracking rollout, ENG-1464 follows up to add automated triage labels in the console.

human_summary: Adds a non-invasive CI adapter that probes prompt robustness to small lexical changes. Ships opt-in with documented configs and CI wiring. Reviewed and merged after minor fixes.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover generators and scoring. Canary run executed on main canary runner against 'instructions' and 'short-qa' cohorts. Observed median extra runtime +12s for a 50-prompt smoke set.
